profileText: a Delegate from New Jersey; born in Philadelphia, Pa., March 22, 1731; attended the common schools; studied law; admitted to the New Jersey bar in 1753 and practiced in the courts of Pennsylvania and New Jersey, with residence in Burlington County, N.J.; member of the New Jersey state general assembly, 1772-1775; member of the committee of correspondence for Burlington County, N.J., in 1774 and 1775; Delegate to the First Continental Congress, 1774; Delegate to the Second Continental Congress, 1775; resigned from the Second Continental Congress effective November 22, 1775; appointed chief justice of the supreme court of New Jersey on November 20, 1789, and served until his death in Burlington, N.J., January 4, 1803; interment in Friends' Burial Ground.

researchRecord.description: A letter from James Kinsey to Robert Morris written on December 19, 1786. In the letter, James Kinsey and his brothers, James and Thomas, assign to Robert Morris the ground rent paid to them by Joshua Byrne. The deed from the Kinseys to Byrne, 1762 May 26, is on the verso.
